summary: Mine Hill's wooden fire tower stood from 1940 to 1989; four cement footings remain on the summit in Auburn, NH, reached by woods roads.

facts.design: Wooden fire lookout tower on the summit
facts.status_note: Wooden tower stood 1940-1989. Four cement footings and other pieces of the tower remain on the summit.

access.note: NH Family Hikes says the tower side of the summit is public property. A private residence occupies one side of the summit clearing. The route crosses Manchester Water Works land.

visit.trail_note: Park at a pull-off on Rt. 121 in Auburn. Unmarked woods roads and paths lead to the summit.

events.note: Wooden fire lookout tower on Mine Hill; the span is given as 1940-1989.
End of the tower's run; the sources do not say how it ended.

notes_for_editor: The Forest Lookouts page for Devil's Den holds only the name and county, with no history. The 1940-1989 span agrees across NH Family Hikes and Wikipedia. The access level rests on NH Family Hikes and a 2025 blog; Manchester Water Works land rules were not checked. The brief names the site Devil's Den (Mine Hill); the state list uses that name for the tower site.
